title: Engineering Quantum Imaging and Ranging in Scattering and Turbulent Environments
content: Quantum imaging and ranging in scattering and turbulent environments require optical, electronic and computational design. This Review analyses photon-pair systems for rain, fog, smoke, atmospheric turbulence and background illumination, with classical correlation and computational single-photon instruments as comparison systems. We explain the functions of photon generation, probe delivery, reference detection, timing electronics and reconstruction, and identify the interfaces through which these modules form an instrument. Propagation and detector models connect optical correlations to acquired counts, frames and arrival times. The engineering analysis examines component matching, spatial encoding, coincidence processing, calibration and coupled photon, timing and latency budgets. Correlation estimators, likelihood-based and Bayesian inference, compressed sensing and learned reconstruction are compared through their information requirements and operating assumptions. Implementations and environmental experiments establish achievable capabilities under specified illumination, acquisition and propagation conditions. Component records, complete-system measurements, theoretical limits and proposed extensions are distinguished to avoid assigning one experiment’s performance to another configuration. We identify research requirements for joint scene–environment estimation, adaptation within channel timescales, reliable reconstruction and integrated instruments. The synthesis provides electrical engineers with a system-level basis for evaluating quantum-imaging implementations, identifying limiting subsystems and assessing the evidence required for practical environmental deployment under realistic optical and computational constraints.
